problem: Sensor-network-guided navigation traditionally needs global positioning (GPS) and an explicit shared map, plus hand-designed multi-hop communication. Prior GNN robot work (e.g. VGAI) only uses local neighborhood information and does not propagate target direction from sensors that see the target to those that don't.
motivation: Low-cost camera sensors with local communication can reduce robot requirements, but requiring positioning and mapping makes deployment cumbersome and not reconfigurable. A learned, positioning-free system that communicates visual features could let all sensors, even those not seeing the target, infer the direction to the target.
key_idea: Train a GNN over a positioning-free network of fisheye-camera sensors by imitating a shortest-path expert so each sensor aggregates neighbors' image features and predicts cost-to-go advantages over discrete directions, with a real-to-sim latent translator for zero-shot sim-to-real.
insight: Communication clearly helps: the no-communication baseline gets SPL 0.492 in the large generalization environment versus 0.742-0.853 with communication, and the SPL gain grows with environment size (1.3x small, 2.0x large). Fully connected communication (D_S=inf) is slightly worse than a local range in the small environment, suggesting locality plus multi-hop gives a better representation than unfiltered aggregation. Mapping real images to the latent encoding of paired simulated images enables zero-shot real transfer.
method: Cost-to-go imitation data: Dijkstra on visibility graphs gives per-direction cost-to-go; the network learns scale-invariant relative advantage vectors A over K discrete directions; 40,000 samples with N=7 sensors, trained with MSE.
Feature extractor: ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 encodes each sensor's omnidirectional RGB image into a 32-d feature that is broadcast to neighbors.

GNN aggregator: message-passing layers (Morris et al. style, W1 self + W2 sum over neighbors) with a disk communication range D_S and L hops, so target information propagates from sensors that see it to all others without any positional information.

Post-processor and policy: an MLP outputs advantages; direction sampled as cat(softmax(-alpha A)) and scaled by beta to a velocity. The robot carries sensor S1 and executes its output; all sensors are trained to increase supervision.

Real-to-sim translator: a CNN maps real fisheye images to the latent encoding phi(o_sim) of the paired simulated image (MSE, phi frozen), trained on 80k pairs from 8 mapped environments; only the encoder is swapped at deployment.
Twin setup: Webots digital twin of a 5.7x4.2 m lab with custom fisheye sensors, DJI RoboMaster, and potential-field collision shielding.

setting.backbone: MobileNetV2 encoder (ImageNet-pretrained) + 1-2 layer GNN + MLP, trained by imitation; real-to-sim translator CNN for real images
setting.training_data: 40,000 simulated environment samples with 7 sensors from Webots with expert cost-to-go labels; 80,000 real/sim image pairs (plus 10,000 test) for the translator
setting.observation: per-sensor omnidirectional (fisheye, equirectangular) RGB, no positioning; robot carries one sensor, plus range sensing for collision shielding
setting.action_space: K discrete directions converted to a velocity command
setting.privileged: none at test time (expert planner with full map only for training labels)

numbers_note: Custom benchmark, no standard benchmark; small test set sizes (52/42 trials). Figure-only results for communication range/sensor count sweeps (large env SPL 0.45 to 0.91) are given in text.
results: Communication between sensors and robot raises SPL up to 2.0x in the large environment (0.45 to 0.91 for L=2, D_S=2) and 1.3x in the small one, beating the communication-free baseline (SR 0.827/SPL 0.719 small, 0.619/0.492 large). Zero-shot real-world transfer achieves 95.7% success and 0.574 SPL over 69 runs.
limitations: No real-world communication-free baseline, and a noticeable reality gap (oscillations, lower SPL) from unaddressed physics gap
Small evaluation sets, custom benchmark, simple 2D cluttered environments with a stationary lab setup; the robot fails if no sensor sees the target
Ideal communication assumed (no asynchrony or delay); requires paired real/sim data with a mocap-mapped environment
builds_on: GNN layer of Morris et al. (Weisfeiler and Leman go neural)
